No usage or adr category is created because neither has content yet; no point-in-time records exist.
evidence: docs/ holds only the installed docs/agents/ files plus the two new indexes; the installed docs/agents/README.md is unchanged and is listed once, from docs/README.md.

The Node.js 24 or 26 prerequisite matches the CLI engines field `>=24 <25 || >=26 <27` and the operations' prerequisite probes; `npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix .repo-standards/runtime` matches the repository-standards skill's documented runtime restore, and .repo-standards/.gitignore ignores runtime/node_modules, so a fresh clone needs it.
CONTRIBUTING.md links docs/development/README.md for prerequisites, local setup and development commands, which now exists.
No package manifest or site code exists, so the guide states that no build or test command exists rather than inventing one.

declarations.explanation: Created the root .gitattributes with one bounded Repo Canon block marking every installed file Linguist would count as linguist-vendored, using exact installed file paths or an installed skill's own directory. The v0.21.0 inventory, derived anew from the installed tree, adds babysit's body-links.mjs and review-outcome.mjs inside the already covered .agents/skills/babysit directory, so the block is unchanged in form. There are no repository-owned lines or repository-owned source files to preserve, and no entry targets .repo-standards/.
evidence: Installed counted files: scripts/validate-issue-contract.mjs, scripts/validate.mjs, operations/lib/rendered-markdown.mjs, .agents/skills/babysit/*.mjs (10 files), .agents/skills/orchestrate/wait.mjs, .agents/skills/triage/ready.mjs and .agents/skills/diagnosing-bugs/scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh; vendor/ and .github/ are default-vendored and need no entry; other installed files are Markdown, YAML, JSON or license text.
`git check-attr linguist-vendored` reports `set` for each of those 16 files; the .claude/skills entries are symlinks and .gitattributes itself is repository-owned, both `unspecified`.
HEAD e80d28a has no .gitattributes, so no repository-owned line existed; the block contains no broad scripts/**, operations/** or .agents/skills/** pattern.

declarations.explanation: The canonical-labels and pull-request-integration fixes ran on lutzseverino/site, authorized by the owner's approval of this adoption on lutzseverino/site#1, and both reported unchanged: all 12 canonical labels already exist with their colors, and squash merging is the only merge method, with PR-title subjects and PR-body messages. Requiring the `PR metadata` check and strict freshness is unavailable, not skipped: the repository is private on a plan that offers neither branch protection nor rulesets, so the next adoption or update requires it once GitHub offers either; unattended merging stays stopped until GitHub enforcement is confirmed. REPO_CANON_RUNS_ON is unset (hosted default). The v0.21.0 rules add internal-review definitions, a default reviewer request bound of 4, PR-body own-head link checks and the policy-file commit rule; none needs project content here, because no reviewer or factory review policy file exists and none was created.
evidence: Fix canonical-labels result: unchanged, GitHub labels already match the canonical configuration for lutzseverino/site. `gh label list` shows needs-triage fbca04, needs-info d4c5f9, ready-for-agent 0e8a16, ready-for-human 1d76db, wontfix ffffff, bug d73a4a, enhancement a2eeef and the five wayfinder labels, plus preserved defaults such as documentation and accessibility.

Fix pull-request-integration result: unchanged; `gh api repos/lutzseverino/site` reads allow_squash_merge true, allow_merge_commit false, allow_rebase_merge false, squash_merge_commit_title PR_TITLE, squash_merge_commit_message PR_BODY.

`gh repo view --json visibility` reports PRIVATE; `gh variable list` returns no variables, so REPO_CANON_RUNS_ON is absent (unset, hosted default); `gh api users/lutzseverino` reports type User, so no organization-level variable can apply.
.github/pull-request-reviewer.json and .github/factory-review-policy.json are absent, which their checks accept.

declarations.explanation: The owner named the licensing: MIT for the code and CC BY 4.0 for the written content (blog posts and other prose), with the copyright notice `Copyright (c) 2026 Jasper Lutz Severino`. The rules allow one root license file only, so the single root LICENSE states both: a header saying which kinds of material each license covers (CC BY 4.0 for the prose the website presents to visitors; MIT for everything else, including source code, configuration, scripts and repository documentation; third-party files under their own notices, such as vendor/ and .agents/skills/, stay under those), then the full MIT License text and the full CC BY 4.0 legal code, each with the owner's copyright notice. No other root license file exists.
evidence: The owner's licensing answer recorded in the earlier v0.20.0 run of this adoption (lutzseverino/site#1): MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for written content, copyright line `Copyright (c) 2026 Jasper Lutz Severino`; this run restores that LICENSE byte for byte.
The MIT text in LICENSE is byte-identical to the MIT text in the Repo Canon source's own LICENSE (.repo-standards/inputs/source/LICENSE).
The CC BY 4.0 text is the official legal code downloaded unchanged from https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.txt.
The repository root holds LICENSE and no other file matching license.* or license-*; the README structure check's license lookup finds exactly LICENSE.

The License link, labelled `MIT and CC BY 4.0`, names the actual repository licenses and targets LICENSE. It mentions no stack, install path or usage example because none exists yet.
